Content: EQUIPMENT MAINTENANCE PROCEDURES Standard Operating Procedure Document ID: SOP-MAINT-001 Version 2.0 - January 2025 ======================================== PURPOSE ======================================== This document outlines the preventive maintenance procedures for all production and material handling equipment at our facility. Proper maintenance ensures: - Equipment reliability and uptime - Worker safety - Cost efficiency - Compliance with regulations - Extended equipment life ======================================== SCOPE ======================================== This procedure applies to: - All production equipment - Material handling equipment (forklifts, pallet jacks) - HVAC systems - Electrical systems - Building infrastructure - Safety equipment ======================================== RESPONSIBILITIES ======================================== MAINTENANCE DEPARTMENT: - Perform scheduled maintenance - Maintain equipment records - Track spare parts inventory - Respond to breakdown calls - Train operators on basic maintenance OPERATORS: - Perform daily inspections - Report equipment issues immediately - Complete basic maintenance tasks - Follow lockout/tagout procedures - Keep equipment clean SUPERVISORS: - Ensure maintenance schedules followed - Approve maintenance requests - Monitor equipment performance - Budget for maintenance needs ======================================== MAINTENANCE CLASSIFICATIONS ======================================== PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE (PM): Scheduled maintenance to prevent failures - Daily operator checks - Weekly inspections - Monthly servicing - Quarterly comprehensive reviews - Annual certifications CORRECTIVE MAINTENANCE: Repairs after equipment failure - Emergency repairs - Breakdown response - Component replacement PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE: Monitoring to predict failures - Vibration analysis - Thermal imaging - Oil analysis - Performance trending ROUTINE MAINTENANCE: Regular upkeep tasks - Cleaning - Lubrication - Adjustments - Minor repairs ======================================== GENERAL MAINTENANCE PROCEDURES ======================================== LOCKOUT/TAGOUT (LOTO): REQUIRED before maintenance on any energized equipment PROCEDURE: 1. Notify affected employees 2. Shut down equipment properly 3. Isolate all energy sources: - Electrical - Hydraulic - Pneumatic - Mechanical - Thermal 4. Apply lockout devices 5. Attach personal danger tag 6. Verify zero energy state 7. Perform maintenance 8. Remove locks only after completion 9. Verify safe operation before restart LOTO REQUIREMENTS: - Personal locks for each worker - "Danger - Do Not Operate" tags - Group lockout for multiple workers - Annual LOTO training required WORK ORDER SYSTEM: All maintenance must have work order CREATING WORK ORDER: 1. Log into maintenance portal 2. Select equipment from dropdown 3. Describe issue in detail 4. Select priority level: - Emergency (safety hazard, complete shutdown) - Urgent (affecting production) - Routine (scheduled PM) - Low (cosmetic, convenience) 5. Attach photos if applicable 6. Submit for approval WORK ORDER TRACKING: - Open: Awaiting assignment - In Progress: Technician working - Parts Ordered: Waiting for materials - On Hold: Pending approval/resources - Completed: Work finished - Closed: Verified and documented ======================================== DAILY OPERATOR INSPECTIONS ======================================== TO BE COMPLETED BEFORE EACH SHIFT FORKLIFT INSPECTION: VISUAL CHECK: □ Check for leaks (oil, coolant, hydraulic) □ Inspect tires for damage or wear □ Check forks for cracks or bends □ Verify all decals and labels present □ Inspect chains and cables □ Check fluid levels OPERATIONAL CHECK: □ Test horn □ Check all lights □ Test brakes □ Verify steering response □ Test hydraulic controls □ Check backup alarm □ Test emergency shut-off IF ANY ISSUES FOUND: 1. Tag equipment "OUT OF SERVICE" 2. Complete deficiency report 3. Notify supervisor immediately 4. Use alternate equipment 5. Do not operate until repaired PRODUCTION EQUIPMENT INSPECTION: BEFORE STARTUP: □ Clear work area □ Check guards and safety devices □ Verify emergency stops function □ Inspect power cords and connections □ Check for unusual noises or vibrations □ Verify all tools and fixtures secure □ Check coolant/lubricant levels DURING OPERATION: □ Monitor for unusual sounds □ Watch for vibration changes □ Check temperature indicators □ Observe product quality □ Monitor cycle times □ Note any error messages AT SHIFT END: □ Clean equipment thoroughly □ Wipe down surfaces □ Remove debris and waste □ Check for loose components □ Report any concerns □ Complete operator log ======================================== PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE SCHEDULES ======================================== WEEKLY MAINTENANCE (Every Monday) FORKLIFTS: - Check battery connections and water levels - Inspect all safety devices - Grease pivot points - Check tire pressure - Inspect hydraulic hoses - Test all lights and horn - Clean air filter PRODUCTION EQUIPMENT: - Lubricate moving parts - Check belt tension - Inspect electrical connections - Clean cooling fans - Check fluid levels - Tighten fasteners - Calibrate if needed MONTHLY MAINTENANCE FORKLIFTS: - Change engine oil and filter - Replace air filter - Inspect brake system - Check hydraulic system thoroughly - Test all safety features - Inspect mast and chains - Document service in logbook PRODUCTION EQUIPMENT: - Deep cleaning - Replace consumables - Precision alignment check - Vibration analysis - Thermal inspection - Update software if needed - Document in equipment history QUARTERLY MAINTENANCE COMPREHENSIVE INSPECTION: - Complete teardown inspection - Replace wear items - Precision measurements - Performance testing - Electrical system check - Hydraulic system service - Bearing inspection and replacement - Chain and cable

MONTHLY MAINTENANCE FORKLIFTS: - Change engine oil and filter - Replace air filter - Inspect brake system - Check hydraulic system thoroughly - Test all safety features - Inspect mast and chains - Document service in logbook PRODUCTION EQUIPMENT: - Deep cleaning - Replace consumables - Precision alignment check - Vibration analysis - Thermal inspection - Update software if needed - Document in equipment history QUARTERLY MAINTENANCE COMPREHENSIVE INSPECTION: - Complete teardown inspection - Replace wear items - Precision measurements - Performance testing - Electrical system check - Hydraulic system service - Bearing inspection and replacement - Chain and cable replacement if worn DOCUMENTATION: - Photograph equipment condition - Update maintenance records - Order replacement parts - Schedule major repairs - Update equipment value ANNUAL MAINTENANCE CERTIFICATION SERVICES: - Complete safety inspection - Load testing (lifting equipment) - Electrical certification - Pressure vessel inspection - Fire suppression system service - Emergency lighting test - Backup power system test MAJOR OVERHAUL: - Replace all wear components - Comprehensive testing - Recalibration - Paint and cosmetic repair - Update specifications - Photograph for insurance ======================================== SPECIFIC EQUIPMENT PROCEDURES ======================================== ELECTRIC FORKLIFT BATTERY MAINTENANCE DAILY: - Check battery charge level - Inspect for damage or corrosion - Verify proper installation WEEKLY: - Check electrolyte levels - Add distilled water if needed (only when fully charged) - Clean terminals - Check voltage MONTHLY: - Perform equalization charge - Check specific gravity of cells - Clean battery compartment - Inspect cables and connections - Document readings BATTERY ROOM PROCEDURES: - Eyewash station accessible - PPE required (face shield, gloves, apron) - Acid spill kit available - No smoking or open flames - Adequate ventilation CHARGING PROCEDURES: 1. Park in designated charging area 2. Turn off forklift 3. Connect charger (red to positive, black to negative) 4. Start charging cycle 5. Monitor for overheating 6. Disconnect when complete 7. Record charge time and date AIR COMPRESSOR MAINTENANCE DAILY: - Check pressure gauge - Drain moisture from tank - Check for leaks - Verify auto-shutoff functions WEEKLY: - Clean air intake filter - Check oil level - Inspect drive belt - Test safety relief valve MONTHLY: - Replace air filter - Change oil (per hours of operation) - Check all connections - Inspect pressure switch - Clean cooling fins QUARTERLY: - Comprehensive leak check - Replace drive belt if worn - Check motor bearings - Test all safety devices - Document condition HVAC SYSTEM MAINTENANCE MONTHLY: - Replace air filters - Check thermostat operation - Inspect condensate drain - Check refrigerant levels - Clean condenser coils QUARTERLY: - Professional service - Check electrical connections - Lubricate motors - Inspect ductwork - Test all controls ANNUALLY: - Complete system inspection - Efficiency testing - Refrigerant leak check - Electrical system check - Clean entire system ======================================== LUBRICATION PROCEDURES ======================================== GENERAL LUBRICATION GUIDELINES: GREASE POINTS: - Identify all grease fittings - Clean fitting before greasing - Use appropriate grease type - Pump until clean grease appears - Wipe excess grease - Document lubrication date LUBRICATION SCHEDULE: - Daily: High-use pivot points - Weekly: General grease points - Monthly: All moving components - Quarterly: Comprehensive lubrication LUBRICANT TYPES: - EP2 Grease: General purpose - High-temp Grease: Over 200°F - Food-grade: Food contact areas - Anti-seize: Threaded connections - Way Oil: Machine slides - Hydraulic Oil: ISO 32 or 46 OIL CHANGES: EQUIPMENT TYPE | INTERVAL | OIL TYPE ---------------|----------|---------- Forklifts | 250 hrs | 10W-30 or 15W-40 Air Compressor | 500 hrs | ISO 46 Synthetic Hydraulic | 1000 hrs | ISO 32 Hydraulic Gearboxes | 2000 hrs | ISO 220 Gear Oil OIL CHANGE PROCEDURE: 1. Run equipment to operating temp 2. Shut down and lockout 3. Position drain pan 4. Remove drain plug 5. Allow complete drainage (30+ min) 6. Replace drain plug and gasket 7. Fill with new oil to proper level 8. Run equipment and check level 9. Check for leaks 10. Document oil change ======================================== SPARE PARTS INVENTORY ======================================== CRITICAL SPARE PARTS (Always in Stock): FORKLIFTS: - Oil filters - Air filters - Hydraulic hoses - Forks (one set) - Drive belts - Fuses - Light bulbs - Batteries (electric) PRODUCTION EQUIPMENT: - Bearings (common sizes) - Belts (V-belts, timing belts) - Electrical components - Sensors and switches - Fuses and circuit breakers - Seals and gaskets - Coolant and lubricants INVENTORY MANAGEMENT: - Minimum stock levels defined - Automatic reorder points - Annual inventory audit - Obsolete parts disposal - Vendor relationships maintained ORDERING PROCEDURE: 1. Check current inventory 2. Obtain part numbers 3. Get quotes from approved vendors 4. Create purchase requisition 5. Obtain approval 6. Place order 7. Track delivery 8. Receive and inspect 9. CORRECTIVE RATIO: Target: 80% preventive, 20% corrective Calculation: (PM Hours / Total Maint Hours) × 100 MAINTENANCE COST PER UNIT: Target: Specific to equipment Calculation: Total Maint Cost / Units Produced REPORTING: - Weekly: Downtime report - Monthly: KPI dashboard - Quarterly: Equipment condition reports - Annually: Maintenance budget review ======================================== DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS ======================================== EQUIPMENT RECORDS: Each piece of equipment must have: - Equipment ID number - Purchase date and cost - Manufacturer specifications - Parts list - Maintenance history - Current condition assessment - Replacement schedule MAINTENANCE LOGS: Document each service including: - Date and time - Type of service - Work performed - Parts replaced - Time spent - Technician name - Next service due date RETENTION POLICY: - Equipment records: Life of equipment + 5 years - Maintenance logs: 7 years - Work orders: 3 years - Inspection reports: 5 years - Warranty documents: Warranty period + 1 year ======================================== SAFETY REQUIREMENTS ======================================== PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT: MINIMUM REQUIRED: - Safety glasses - Steel-toed boots - Hearing protection (if over 85 dB) - Work gloves TASK-SPECIFIC: - Welding: Welding helmet, leather gloves - Chemical: Chemical-resistant gloves, face shield - Electrical: Insulated gloves, arc-rated clothing - Confined Space: Respirator, harness CONFINED SPACE ENTRY: Required for tanks, pits, vessels PROCEDURE: 1. Obtain entry permit 2. Test atmosphere (O2, LEL, toxic gases) 3. Establish ventilation 4. Post attendant at entrance 5. Use retrieval equipment 6. Maintain communication 7. Emergency rescue plan ready ELECTRICAL SAFETY: - Qualified electrician only - Lockout/tagout required - Insulated tools - Arc-rated PPE - No energized work unless justified ======================================== EMERGENCY MAINTENANCE PROCEDURES ======================================== EQUIPMENT FAILURE DURING OPERATION: IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: 1. Press emergency stop 2. Secure work area 3. Evacuate if dangerous 4. Call maintenance (Extension 5100) 5. Notify supervisor 6. Complete incident report PRIORITY RESPONSE: - Safety hazards: Within 15 minutes - Production stoppage: Within 30 minutes - Partial operation: Within 2 hours - Non-critical: Next business day TEMPORARY REPAIRS: - Authorized only if safe - Document temporary fix - Schedule permanent repair - Monitor closely - Post warning signs EQUIPMENT REPLACEMENT CRITERIA: Consider replacement when: - Repair cost > 50% of replacement cost - Frequent breakdowns (3+ per month) - Parts no longer available - Safety cannot be assured - Technology obsolete - Maintenance cost exceeds depreciation ======================================== TRAINING REQUIREMENTS ======================================== MAINTENANCE TECHNICIANS: INITIAL TRAINING: - Safety procedures (40 hours) - Equipment-specific training - Lockout/tagout certification - Confined space entry - Forklift certification - Electrical safety (if applicable) - Hydraulic systems CONTINUING EDUCATION: - Annual safety refresher - New equipment training - Advanced diagnostics - Manufacturer certifications - Industry conferences OPERATORS: REQUIRED TRAINING: - Daily inspection procedures - Basic troubleshooting - When to call maintenance - Lockout/tagout awareness - Equipment-specific operation ANNUAL REVIEW: - Safety procedures - Inspection checklist updates - New equipment orientation - Best practices ======================================== VENDOR MANAGEMENT ======================================== APPROVED VENDORS: Maintain list of qualified vendors for: - Parts suppliers - Service providers - Specialty repairs - Emergency services VENDOR QUALIFICATION: - Insurance verification - License validation - Reference checks - Pricing agreements - Service level agreements SERVICE CONTRACTS: - Annual HVAC maintenance - Fire suppression inspection - Elevator service - Boiler inspection - Emergency generator testing ======================================== CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT ======================================== MONTHLY REVIEW MEETINGS: Discuss: - Recent failures and root causes - Schedule compliance - Budget vs. actual costs - Safety incidents - Process improvements IMPROVEMENT INITIATIVES: - Operator feedback - New technology evaluation - Efficiency improvements - Cost reduction opportunities - Reliability enhancements ======================================== REVISION HISTORY ======================================== Version 2.0 - January 2025 - Added predictive maintenance section -
